title: Retail Roundup: Mobile Shopping Surge, Walmart Steps Back in Brazil - Wiredfocus
text:
Retail Roundup: Mobile Shopping Surge, Walmart Steps Back in Brazil June 4, 2018
Not that long ago, the dominant narrative was that millennials and Amazon.com (AMZN) were causing the death of traditional retail. But that’s far from the case, says Marissa Tarleton , chief marketing officer at deals and coupon aggregator RetailMeNot .
Tarleton told Barron’s that RetailMeNot’s 20 million monthly users are proof that traditional retailers that are willing to harness mobile use to drive sales can compete in today’s market place. “We used to talk about mobile commerce, and now we talk about mobile influence–mobile is now the way for brands to capture consumers’ [attention] when they’re browsing,” in store or before they even leave the house.
RetailMeNot’s data show that 62% of its users are utilizing its app while they’re shopping in brick-and-mortar stores, and plenty of those are millennials: 69% of shoppers in that cohort “will not complete a purchase without an offer or deal,” above (but not that dissimilar to) other age brackets. “The savings mindset is a significant one for millennials; it’s not saving because they need to, but because they want to, because they want to be smart about how they use their money.”
Even though millennials may be hooked on their smartphones comparing prices, they’re not just doing it on their couches: A full 80% still choose to go to a store, again, not that dissimilar to percentages for other generations. (Perhaps not surprising, given that price-conscious shoppers know that Amazon isn’t necessarily the cheapest retailer for many items any more, just one of major convenience.) Tarleton says that this not only disproves the idea that all physical stores are going away, but that retailers that can build savvy tech solutions to improve in-store experiences and drive traffic have an advantage. “One of the biggest advantages Amazon doesn’t have at scale is a store front; traditional retailers have the benefit of real estate and physical stores that consumers are still asking for, how they use it, how they innovate with mobile to engage, drive foot traffic, and personalize offerings is the question.” READ Mobile police investigate report of woman drugged, kidnapped by acquaintance
Mobile is an increasingly popular way to boost customer engagement, she says–and plenty of retailers that partner with RetailMeNot can use it as a shortcut to build relationships with consumers without using their own resources to build out their tech offerings.
Just as importantly, she notes that one of the silver linings to the shakeup in retail is that companies are finally taking the time to understand what their consumers need and change accordingly. “I’m excited that a lot of retailers really listening to their customers and building customer-first strategies,” Tarleton says, from adding off-price and factory outlets to their portfolios to create more “buy online for store pickup” availability. Those that create experiences and options that allow consumers to shop whenever and however they want will be the most successful.
* Analyst Moves
Loop Capital’s Anthony Chukumba downgraded Big Lots (BIG) from Buy to Hold, and shaved $20 from his price target to $40, following its first-quarter earnings report . He writes that the results show the retailer got off to a bad start for the year, and he was “particularly disturbed” by the comparable-store-sales decline, the ongoing slowdown in furniture sales, and the fact that the disappointment came in the first quarter without its former chief executive.
Not that the shares are suffering much today: Big Lots is up 4.4% after Friday’s dip.
Telsey Advisory Group’s Joseph Feldman reiterated a Market Perform rating on the shares today, but also lowered his price target by $7 to $42. He writes that despite some positives in the quarter, including several strategic initiatives, in the near term the Street is likely to still view the shares as a “show me” story.
*
Speaking of stocks that Chukumba lacks enthusiasm in, he doesn’t see much to get excited about in terms of Dollar General (DG), which also reported earnings last week . He believes that the “non-existent” spring in many parts of the country hurt the discounter, as it did so many other retailers, meaning the disappointment wasn’t as bad as it appears at first blush, especially since trends have improved along with the weather–but not enough for him to get bullish on the shares, hence his Hold rating and $97 price target. He also has a Hold rating and $14 price target on GameStop (GME), writing that there’s “no reason to become more constructive on the stock” now, especially as the full year’s results likely to be weighed to the back half (even more so than usual). Ulta Beauty (ULTA) is another Hold rating for him: Even though the company got off to the strong start for the year , he warns that same-store sales are sequentially declining and the stock looks fully valued. He has a $250 price target on the shares. Other News
Walmart (WMT) is trading higher today on news that Advent International will invest a majority stake in Walmart Brazil. The private-equity firm will control 80% of the retailer’s Brazilian arm, with Walmart retaining a 20% sake. Moody’s Investor Service analyst Charlie O’Shea writes that the move is consistent with its strategy to redeploy capital and personnel to areas where it has strong longer-term potential. “Similar to the Asda divestiture in the UK, this decision regarding Brazil continues the repositioning of International assets, and enables the company to make investments such as the Flipkart transaction in India.”
Walmart also held its investor day on Friday, and analysts subsequently weighed in. Telsey Advisory’s Dana Tesley reiterated an Outperform rating and $105 price target on the shares, writing that Walmart is one of the few retailers that will successfully adapt to an omnichannel model, thanks to its strong management team and financial flexibility. ” Walmart has been exerting its dominance in physical retail and generating new prowess in digital commerce, which should support a premium valuation for the stock.” READ Chase Mobile updated with iPhone X optimization & more
Stephens’ Ben Bienvenu reiterated an Overweight rating on Walmart and $108 price target, writing that the company is making the changes needed to compete over the long term. Even if they recent moves are dilutive at first, they will pay off over time. He also likes management’s cost control, a decision to invest in employees , and improvement in the in-store experience.
*
Amazon share are higher, unfazed by news that it was among several big tech firms, including Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT), that bought user data from Facebook (FB), although the latter is falling. Read more about it on Tech Trader Daily .
*
Credit Suisse’s Seth Sigman takes a look at low-income consumer wage data for last month, writing that pay improved in May, which bodes well for the second quarter.
Among the biggest winners from this trend is AutoZone (AZO), Sigman writes, which is more leveraged to an improvement to the do-it-yourself consumer than O’Reilly Automotive (ORLY) and Advance Auto Parts (AAP). “This wage data is also a key input in our Auto Parts annual-demand model, which along with a gradually improving vehicle “sweet spot” should point to improving trends in the second half of 2018,” he writes, while acknowledging that a slow start to the year has fueled debate.
Dollar stores also tend to benefit from rising-wage trends for low earners, although he warns that internal struggles at Dollar Tree’s (DLTR) Family Dollar unit will likely outweigh this tailwind. Moreover, dollar-store managements said last week that sales were improving as weather warmed, and if consumers have more money in their pockets, that could signal a positive shift in the discretionary categories.
